methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Waabi, a Series C autonomous transportation company founded by Raquel Urtasun, operates within a sector containing 8 identifiable private peers including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia. No public comparables exist in this subsegment, limiting peer-based valuation approaches.

The analysis applies stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation technique given data constraints. Using total capital raised of $1.0B as a valuation proxy, a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C advancement yields an implied valuation of $1.7B. A peer-median approach was not feasible; while 3 same-sector companies exist, insufficient datapoints met narrow stage and valuation-tier filters necessary for statistical reliability.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.4B to $2.0B, with a median point of $1.7B. This derivation rests on a single method and relies on capital raised as a proxy for post-money valuation, which may not reflect market conditions at investment timing or capital efficiency. Key uncertainties include the applicability of stage-progression multiples to frontier transportation technology, where risk and development timelines diverge significantly from conventional software startups. Additional data on comparable Series C or D closings in autonomous vehicle or transportation software would strengthen confidence in this range.
